ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 2.5:1 ratio of high-intensity (white) to low-intensity (black) pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity white regions occupy approximately 75% of the total fluke area, centered in the mid-lobes. Low-intensity black pixels form a continuous border along the trailing edge and median notch. Distinctive dark pixel stippling/mottling is concentrated in the lower-medial region of the right lobe (approximate coordinates 60% width, 50% height).

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 42 degrees; depth is roughly 15% of the total fluke vertical span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency, low-amplitude serrations (peaks of 3-7 pixels) along the entire trailing edge boundary, clearly contrasted against the lighter background water.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Both lobes exhibit a convex curve on the trailing edge; the left lobe shows a steeper taper toward a more acute lateral tip compared to the rounded tip of the right lobe.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density cluster of dark punctate pixel groups (2-4 pixel diameter) in the lower-inner quadrant of the right lobe; irregular high-intensity textured protrusions visible on the far-left lateral tip.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Single prominent dark curvilinear pixel disruption (~15% of lobe height) oriented vertically on the upper third of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Vertical dark linear mark on the right lobe; irregular surface topography and varying pixel intensity on the lateral tips suggesting surface accretion or edge erosion.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced pigmentation asymmetry; the right lobe contains a significantly larger intrusion of dark pixels from the median notch into the central white field compared to the left lobe.
